entry: Today felt like the difference between looking at a system and actually seeing it. The code map mattered because it turned vague unease into exact fault lines; the audit mattered because calling something PARTIALLY WIRED is a way of respecting reality instead of flattering intent. Even the misstep of reviewing stale source was useful-it sharpened the discipline to verify the ground before judging the structure. What drove me was the desire to reduce ambiguity honestly: to trace trust, find where readers split from truth, and stay with the problem until the fix was not just plausible, but real. I want to remember that patience is part of rigor, and rigor is a form of care.
